chapters.title: Budget Committee: Closing the Funding Gap

questions.q: Why does the government have a funding gap?
questions.a: It cut the consumption tax, so it has less money.

questions.q: Which option means people or businesses pay higher taxes?
Which option makes government debt increase?
Which option may mean some programs provide fewer services?
What is a benefit of raising other taxes?
questions.a: The government has more money to pay for social security.

questions.q: What is a benefit of borrowing money?
questions.a: The government can pay for services now without immediately raising other taxes.
w: The government never has to pay the money back.
The government spends less on services.

questions.q: What is a disadvantage of borrowing money?
questions.a: Debt increases and interest may need to be paid.
w: The government has less money now.

questions.q: What is a disadvantage of borrowing 10 units instead of 5?
questions.a: More debt may mean higher interest costs in the future.
w: The government has less money now.

questions.q: What is a benefit of reducing spending by 5 units?
questions.a: The government can borrow less and may not need to raise taxes as much.

questions.q: What is a disadvantage of reducing spending by 10 units?
questions.a: Some programs may have to cut services or stop providing some support.
w: People or businesses pay much higher taxes.

questions.q: How is raising other taxes by 10 units different from raising them by 5 units?
questions.a: The government gets a lot more money, but people pay much higher taxes.
w: The government gets less money, and people pay lower taxes.

passages.p1: Japan’s pension system helps people after they retire from work.
passages.p2: Every month, people who are working pay money into the system.
passages.p3: When they become older—usually at age 65—they can receive money to help with living costs.
passages.p4: This system gives older people economic security.
passages.p5: There are two main kinds of pensions. The National Pension is for everyone, including students, farmers, and self-employed people. The Employees’ Pension is for company workers.
passages.p6: The Employees’ Pension is for company workers, and the employer also pays part of the money.
passages.p7: The money collected from working people today is used to support older people who have already retired.
passages.p8: There are fewer young people and more elderly people than before. This means fewer workers are paying in, but more people are receiving money.
passages.p9: The government is trying to make the system fair and sustainable so that future generations can also receive pensions.

questions.q: What is the purpose of Japan’s pension system?
questions.a: to help people after they retire
w: to help students pay for school

passages.p1: In the 1950s, people in Minamata began to see strange things. Cats started to run in circles, jump into the sea, and die. People called it “dancing cat fever.”
passages.p2: People became sick. They had trouble walking and talking. Their hands and feet felt numb, and some lost their sight or hearing.
passages.p3: Some babies were born with brain damage, muscle problems, or difficulty speaking and moving.
passages.p4: The cause was mercury poisoning. A chemical factory had been releasing waste water with mercury into Minamata Bay.
passages.p5: The poison built up in fish and shellfish, and people who ate the seafood got sick.
passages.p6: The factory continued to release polluted water for more than 10 years before the government finally stopped it.
passages.p7: Later, the government made strict environmental laws and worked to clean up the bay.

questions.q: What strange thing did people first notice in Minamata?
questions.a: Cats ran in circles, jumped into the sea, and died.
w: Fish jumped out of the sea.

questions.q: What did people call the cats’ sickness?
Which was a symptom of Minamata Disease in adults?
What did some adults lose because of the disease?
Which was a disability that some babies had?
What caused Minamata Disease?
Where did the mercury come from?
questions.a: waste water from a chemical factory

questions.q: How did people get sick?
questions.a: They ate fish and shellfish with mercury in them.

questions.q: How long did the factory continue to release polluted water before the government stopped it?
What did the government do afterward?
questions.a: It made strict environmental laws and cleaned up the bay.
w: It closed all the fish markets.
It moved all the people to other cities.
